source.title: Understanding Generalization in the Interpolation Regime using the Rate Function
source.authors: Andrés R. Masegosa; Luis A. Ortega

record.tranche_reason: The study trains convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 and reports training accuracy across training recipes and model sizes, conceptually testing whether training reaches interpolation and how width affects it.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. for prior memorization results; those cited results are not rows. Rows below cover the paper's own reported training-accuracy results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own CIFAR-10 training classification accuracies after gradient training, including random labels, using the same method and measure as V1's original experiments. Its main purpose is studying generalization, but these training results directly test V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors claim their distribution-dependent PAC-Chernoff bound is tight for interpolators and that sufficiently smoother interpolators, under their rate-function definition and theorem conditions, generalize better. They connect this framework to regularization, invariance, augmentation, and over-parameterization. The reported 395k-and-larger models reach 100% training accuracy, but optimization success is supplementary evidence; the paper explicitly leaves SGD's role in finding good interpolators unexplored.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CIFAR-10 training and SGD, with the paper's own Inception and convolutional-network recipes; does not report an explicit replication of the claim's cited studies. The experiments vary regularization, augmentation, random labels, pixel shuffling, and model size.
record.method_sensitivity: Training accuracy changes with model size in the Figure 6 sweep: it rises from 43.82% at 4k parameters to 100.0% at 395k and above. Figure 2 recipes, including random labels, all report near-perfect training accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Trained MLPs achieve 99.99% training accuracy with and without fixed pixel shuffling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient training can reach near-zero CIFAR-10 training classification error in the tested fully connected networks.

record.problems: Training accuracy is reported for CIFAR-10 only. Uncertainty estimates are not reported. The Figure 6 stopping rule allows stopping after two consecutive epochs without improvement for the smallest models.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, Adam, intermediate label-corruption levels, systematic variation of stopping time, and regularized recipes that leave substantial training error. The size sweep does not separate insufficient capacity from plateau stopping.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious-minimum frequencies, and one- or two-neuron student surplus.
Depth-dependent training degradation and comparisons with identity shortcuts, very deep tanh initialization, or Fixup.
Effects of initialization on training speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature evolution, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Matched comparisons of training speed and learning-rate tolerance with and without batch normalization or Fixup.

missing.what: Figure 11 describes an Inception trained with translation and rotation augmentation achieving nearly perfect interpolation. Record its training-loss result separately, preserving the approximate wording and distinguishing augmented loss from classification error.
missing.locator: Section 7.2, Figure 11 discussion; Appendix A.1, Figures 9 and 11
missing.versions: V1: supplementary training-loss evidence; exact training classification accuracy is not supplied.

record.verdict_notes: Low accuracy in small models supports an explicit qualification already present in V1, so it does not warrant a challenge or an additional scope limitation. The presence of batch normalization and He initialization alone does not test V6 or V4. The paper's rate-function smoothness concerns generalization and does not measure V5's training-loss curvature.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, Adam, early stopping as a varied condition, and comparisons among initialization schemes are not tested.
